body: docTR (Document Text Recognition) - a seamless, high-performing & accessible library for OCR-related tasks powered by Deep Learning. Ongoing development and maintenance by t2k.
plain_description: The big picture: docTR turns documents into structured data with deep-learning OCR that anyone can use — no AI expertise required. Here's why it matters: extract text from PDFs, images, and web pages with state-of-the-art accuracy, then integrate results via a simple API or Docker container. The bottom line: go from paper to searchable, usable data in minutes.
technical_description: docTR is an open-source document text recognition (OCR) library built on PyTorch. It provides a two-stage pipeline combining text detection (localizing words) and text recognition (identifying characters), with support for document layout analysis and key information extraction. The library offers multiple pretrained model architectures for detection (DBNet, LinkNet, FAST) and recognition (CRNN, SAR, MASTER, ViTSTR, PARSeq, VIPTR), deployable via Python API, FastAPI-based REST service, or Docker container with CUDA GPU acceleration.
title: docTR

body: Ready-to-use OCR with 80+ supported languages and all popular writing scripts including Latin, Chinese, Arabic, Devanagari, Cyrillic and etc.
plain_description: The big picture: extract text from images in 80+ languages with a single line of Python — no machine learning expertise needed. Here's why it matters: automate document processing, receipt scanning, and data entry for any business workflow. The bottom line: turn any image into searchable, usable text data instantly.
technical_description: EasyOCR is a Python library for optical character recognition (OCR) supporting 80+ languages and multiple writing scripts. It uses a PyTorch-based deep learning pipeline with CRAFT for text detection and CRNN (ResNet/VGG + LSTM + CTC) for recognition. The library provides a simple Python API and command-line interface, auto-downloads pretrained models from a model hub, and runs on CPU or NVIDIA GPU via CUDA. Installation is through pip, with a Dockerfile available for containerized deployment.
title: EasyOCR

body: pix2tex: Using a ViT to convert images of equations into LaTeX code.
plain_description: Turn screenshots of math equations into LaTeX code instantly — no more manual equation typing. Researchers, students, and technical writers save hours by snapping a picture or screenshot and getting accurate LaTeX output. The tool works from your clipboard, files, or a simple desktop GUI.
technical_description: pix2tex is a Python-based OCR system that converts images of mathematical equations into LaTeX code. It uses a Vision Transformer (ViT) encoder with a ResNet backbone paired with a Transformer decoder to generate token sequences. The package provides multiple interfaces: a CLI tool, a GUI application (latexocr) for screenshot-based capture, a Python API, and a Streamlit web demo. Docker images are available for containerized deployment. Pre-trained model checkpoints are downloaded automatically. Training is supported via a custom dataset pipeline using XeLaTeX-rendered images and a configurable tokenizer.
title: LaTeX OCR

body: Convert PDF to markdown + JSON quickly with high accuracy
plain_description: Save thousands of hours by automatically converting PDFs, Word docs, Excel sheets, and more into clean, usable formats. Marker preserves tables, equations, images, and document structure — so your team processes documents in seconds instead of hours. The bottom line: faster document workflows mean more time for analysis, not formatting.
technical_description: Marker is a Python-based document conversion pipeline that transforms PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, EPUB, and image files into markdown, JSON, HTML, or chunk-based output. It uses the surya VLM for layout detection and OCR, served by a local inference server (vLLM on NVIDIA GPU, llama.cpp on CPU/Apple Silicon), alongside lightweight CPU models for text extraction and layout analysis. The pipeline optionally integrates LLMs (Gemini, Claude, OpenAI, Ollama, etc.) for enhanced accuracy on complex layouts, tables, and inline math. Marker is extensible through custom processors, renderers, and providers, and includes a FastAPI-based REST API server for remote conversion.
title: Marker

body: Turn any PDF or image document into structured data for your AI. A powerful, lightweight OCR toolkit that bridges the gap between images/PDFs and LLMs. Supports 100+ languages.
plain_description: The big picture: PaddleOCR converts any PDF or image into clean, structured data your AI systems can use immediately. Why it matters: No more manual data entry or complex document workflows — just feed in documents and get JSON or Markdown output ready for RAG, AI agents, and automation. The bottom line: With 100+ language support and deep integration with Dify, RAGFlow, and other platforms, it's the fastest way to make your documents AI-ready.
technical_description: PaddleOCR is a lightweight OCR toolkit and document AI engine for converting PDFs and images into structured JSON or Markdown output. It provides a modular pipeline architecture supporting text detection, recognition, layout analysis, table extraction, formula recognition, and seal detection across 100+ languages. The project includes multiple model series: PP-OCRv6 for universal scene text recognition (50 languages, single model), PaddleOCR-VL for vision-language document parsing (0.9B parameters, 96.3% accuracy), and PP-StructureV3 for structure-aware document conversion with fine-grained element coordinates. Deployment options include Python SDK, Docker containers, C++ inference, REST API serving via hubserving, Android/iOS mobile runtimes, and browser inference via PaddleOCR.js. Models can be exported to ONNX format and accelerated using OpenVINO, TensorRT, or ONNX Runtime on CPU, NVIDIA GPU, or Apple Silicon.
title: PaddleOCR

body: OCR, layout analysis, reading order, table recognition in 90+ languages
plain_description: Extract text, layout, and tables from any document in 90+ languages with state-of-the-art accuracy. The big picture: Surya turns messy PDFs, scans, and images into clean, structured data — without needing a massive GPU cluster. It handles dense academic papers, handwritten forms, multilingual documents, and complex tables in a single pass. The bottom line: you get production-grade OCR at 5 pages per second on a single GPU, with output you can feed directly into downstream systems.
technical_description: Surya is a 650M-parameter vision-language model for document OCR, layout analysis, reading-order detection, and table recognition. It runs a single shared VLM served by vllm (NVIDIA GPU) or llama.cpp (CPU/Apple Silicon), with a separate torch-based text-line detection model. The Python library provides CLI commands (surya_ocr, surya_layout, surya_table, surya_detect) and a programmatic API via SuryaInferenceManager with RecognitionPredictor, LayoutPredictor, TableRecPredictor, and DetectionPredictor classes. Output is returned as structured JSON with per-block polygons, bboxes, confidence scores, and HTML content (including <math> tags for equations and <table> for recognized tables). The inference manager auto-spawns the backend server or can attach to a pre-running OpenAI-compatible endpoint via SURYA_INFERENCE_URL. A streamlit-based GUI is included for interactive exploration.
title: Surya

body: Tesseract Open Source OCR Engine (main repository)
plain_description: Tesseract is a free open-source OCR engine that extracts text from scanned documents, PDFs, and images so you never need to retype a single word. It supports over 100 languages out of the box and exports to plain text, searchable PDF, HTML, and more. The bottom line: automate document digitization and eliminate manual data entry.
technical_description: Tesseract is an open-source OCR engine that provides libtesseract, a C/C++ library, and a command-line tool for optical character recognition. The engine implements a legacy character-pattern recognizer alongside an LSTM-based neural network for line-level recognition. It supports Unicode (UTF-8), over 100 languages, multiple image input formats (PNG, JPEG, TIFF), and output formats including plain text, hOCR (HTML), PDF, TSV, ALTO, and PAGE. Integration is via the C API (capi.h) or C++ API (baseapi.h) with community-maintained bindings for other languages. The engine uses Leptonica for image input and supports training custom character sets for the neural net recognizer.
title: Tesseract OCR

body: Pure Javascript OCR for more than 100 Languages 📖🎉🖥
plain_description: Extract text from images in over 100 languages with a pure JavaScript library that runs anywhere — no server or GPU required. Add OCR to your web app or Node service with a single npm install or script tag. The big picture: bring the power of Tesseract to your frontend or backend without any native dependencies.
technical_description: Tesseract.js is a JavaScript library that ports the Tesseract OCR engine to the browser and Node.js by wrapping a WebAssembly port (tesseract.js-core). It provides a worker-based async API for recognizing text from images, supporting over 100 languages and multiple output formats (plain text, hOCR, word/symbol blocks). The library can be installed via npm/yarn for Node.js or loaded via CDN script tag or ESM import for browser use. It offers parallel processing via schedulers, rotation preprocessing, and works with common image formats. It does not support PDF input or modify the underlying Tesseract recognition model.
title: Tesseract.js
